dedupe_keys.name: the impact of critical water levels on container inland waterway transport

description: Bedoya-Maya, Felipe and colleagues publish this resource through the source community. A time-series econometric study relates monthly container throughput to low/high-water navigability restrictions along the Rhine during 2000–2022, controlling for confounding factors. Coverage includes spatial variation, lagged effects and changes after 2018. Reported average losses increase when disruptions persist beyond 24 days. The study also estimates conditional 2050 annual-average losses; these are model projections, not observed future outcomes. The deposited paper does not establish public access to the complete panel or fitted code. Zenodo supplies the descriptive publication with open access under cc-by-4.0. The publication does not establish public access to an implementation or its separate licence. A limitation is that complete implementation or measurement settings cannot be reconstructed from descriptive metadata alone. Related experimental components and publications retain their distinct roles; separate deposits are not assumed to provide independent observations. The analysis concerns waterway resilience to low and high water levels.
